Plan a nitrogen rate for a grain crop

Source: R/plan-nitrogen-rate.R
plan_nitrogen_rate.Rd

The canonical grain decision: choose how much nitrogen to apply to a crop by expected profit, abstaining to the status-quo rate when the yield evidence is unverified or no rate is clearly better. It is a grain-semantics wrapper over decideR::decide_input_rate() – the profit maximisation, the grounding firewall, and the abstention logic are decideR's; grainPlan supplies the grain economics (n_rate_economics()), the crop context, a grower-facing rationale, and the grain_decision result.

Usage

plan_nitrogen_rate(
  yield_draws,
  rates,
  price_grain,
  price_n,
  crop = "wheat",
  grounding = decideR::grounding_unverified(),
  safe_rate = 0,
  decisive_prob = 0.6,
  ...
)

Arguments

yield_draws

A numeric matrix of posterior yield draws, one column per candidate rate (rows are draws).

rates

A numeric vector of candidate nitrogen rates, one per column of yield_draws.

price_grain

The grain price per unit yield (passed to n_rate_economics()).

price_n

The nitrogen price per unit rate (passed to n_rate_economics()).

crop

The crop the decision concerns (default "wheat").

grounding

One or more grounding tokens for the yield evidence; combined worst-case and passed to the decision engine.

safe_rate

The fallback rate on abstention (default 0, the no-input status quo).

decisive_prob

Minimum posterior probability that the leading rate beats the status quo (passed to decideR::decide()).

...

Further arguments passed to the decision core (e.g. min_ess). constraint is rejected with an error: decideR::decide_input_rate() does not honour a rate constraint and would otherwise drop it silently (use plan_nitrogen_rate_from_manifest(), which does honour one, or cap rates before calling).

Value

A grain_decision of kind "nitrogen_rate" whose action is the recommended rate.

Details

Pass either a yield-draws matrix (yield_draws, one column per candidate rate, rows are posterior draws – the object a PESTO inversion or a mechanistic yield-response posterior produces) together with rates, or an upstream orchestra_manifest to plan_nitrogen_rate_from_manifest(), which sources the draws and the grounding token straight from the manifest. Either way the grounding rides from the evidence through the decision: an unverified yield posterior forces the status-quo rate, never a confident wrong recommendation.

See also

plan_nitrogen_rate_from_manifest() for the manifest entry point; n_rate_economics() for the economics; decideR::decide_input_rate() for the underlying engine.

Other grain-decisions: plan_grade_target(), plan_nitrogen_rate_from_manifest(), plan_variety(), plan_variety_from_manifest()

Examples

set.seed(1L)
rates <- seq(0, 200, by = 25)
# diminishing-returns yield response with posterior noise
mu <- 3 + 2.5 * (1 - exp(-rates / 80))
yield_draws <- vapply(mu, function(m) rnorm(1500L, m, 0.3), numeric(1500L))
plan_nitrogen_rate(yield_draws, rates, price_grain = 350, price_n = 1.3,
                   crop = "wheat",
                   grounding = decideR::grounding_grounded())
#> <grain_decision> RECOMMENDED  [grounded]
#>   crop   : wheat
#>   kind   : nitrogen_rate
#>   action : 175 kg N/ha
#>   why    : Apply 175 kg N/ha to the wheat crop: it maximises expected profit ($1596.9/unit area) and clearly beats the status quo on the posterior.
